findings.title: beta-branding.ts BETA_HEADERS_BLOCK appends a second `/*` rule that replaces the CSP / X-Frame-Options / HSTS / Permissions-Policy rule on beta.xivdyetools.app
findings.rationale: public/_headers:7 is the only `/*` rule; beta-branding.ts:38-52 appends another `/*` whose doc comment wrongly claims Pages merges identical patterns. Pages keys rules by path, so the later one wins, and the live probe shows beta serving no CSP/XFO/HSTS. The referrer-policy and nosniff it does return are Pages defaults. This is a live regression of a security control on a public origin that allows sign-in and preset writes, so clickjacking works there today. check-beta-build.js only greps for the string, so the fix is trivial: merge X-Robots-Tag into the existing rule and assert the served headers.

refuter.reason:
I could not refute it, and no earlier verdict or accepted trade-off covers it.

- **The entry is live.** apps/oauth/src/constants/oauth.ts:17 still lists 'https://xivdyetools.projectgalatine.com' in ALLOWED_REDIRECT_ORIGINS. In production, getAllowedRedirectOrigins strips only the localhost entries, so this one survives.
- **Both checks use it.** The redirect check (oauth-flow.ts:95, 150-154, 278) and the CORS check (index.ts:73) read that list.
- **The old route is still bound.** wrangler.toml:7-8 keeps auth.xivdyetools.projectgalatine.com as a custom domain on the production worker. oauth has no [env.production], so its top-level block is production.
- **Nothing accepts it.** docs/architecture/security-trade-offs.md says nothing about it. The 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-15 reports list only a general "exact-origin allowlist" as a positive control. The 2026-08-21 rejected item is generic open redirect, not this entry.
- **The project calls it removable.** docs/operations/DOMAIN_DEPRECATION.md Phase 1 says removing it is "landable immediately" and calls these entries "already dead in practice". The old deploy blocker (the 5.0 merge) is no longer relevant.

Why LOW and not higher:
- **The attack needs the domain.** It works only if someone other than the maintainer controls the xivdyetools.projectgalatine.com origin. Today that host is the maintainer's own Pages project: functions/_middleware.ts:17-21 matches that hostname and returns a 301. That is the same reasoning the 2026-08-21 audit used for OAUTH-6, where a branch alias on the owner's Pages project was "not hijackable while that project exists".
- **Losing the domain is unlikely.** projectgalatine.com is also the maintainer's Bluesky identity, and FINDING-030 records that zone as still in use.
- **The impact would be real.** If the domain were lost, the new owner could start a login with their own PKCE challenge and receive the victim's code through the signed bounce. They could then exchange it for that user's JWT.
- **The CORS half adds nothing.** Auth is bearer-only and no cookies are set, so the CORS entry gives no extra access.
- **The bound route adds nothing either.** It is the same worker, so it is extra surface, not a separate exploit.

I could not refute the code defect, but the language half of the claim does not apply to production.

What the code does:
- resetPreference with no key runs only kv.delete(buildPrefsKey(userId)) (apps/discord-worker/src/services/preferences.ts:314-317).

Narrowing:
- apps/discord-worker/CHANGELOG.md:553 records that cleanup-v4-kv.ts ran against production on 2026-08-29 and that "no i18n:user:* keys existed".
- Nothing writes that prefix any more (moderation-worker/src/services/i18n.ts:28 and the grep agree). So language re-migration cannot happen on production.

What remains:
- The world key can still come back. The same changelog line says the budget:world:v1:* sweep was deliberately left out and is "a product decision" (DEAD-010).
- Its writer was user-preferences.ts. It was already dead code in the 2026-02-28 audit (DEAD-020) and was removed in 0a147474, so any surviving keys date from before then.
- Running `wrangler kv key list --prefix budget:world:v1:` against the production KV namespace (1fcb7e037ccd4172a47fccd97cf8e753) would settle whether the bug can be triggered. If the list is empty, the finding is unreachable and should be REJECTED/INFO.

Prior audits:
- Neither the 2026-08-29 nor the 2026-09-15 security report, nor docs/architecture/security-trade-offs.md, accepts or rejects this reset behavior.
- DEAD-010 kept the migration for compatibility only and never considered what reset does with it.

Impact:
- Some legacy users would see their world/data-center preference come back after /preferences reset. That breaks the "Until you reset them" promise in PRIVACY_POLICY.md:28 and :146.
- The value is not personal: a game server name keyed by the already-disclosed Discord user ID. LOW is the ceiling, and INFO if the KV list comes back empty.

Policy: NONE, reconcile_case 0. Fix: delete budget:world:v1:<id> (and i18n:user:<id>) on reset, or after a successful migration put. Rotation: NONE.

The omission is real. apps/web-app/PRIVACY.md:83-95 (§Links that take you to other sites) names only the Glamour Reader "Open in…" item links and the dye-card market/database links. apps/web-app/TERMS_OF_SERVICE.md:89-101 (§Other people's services) lists the same two families. Meanwhile apps/web-app/src/components/v4/preset-detail.ts:986-998 binds the author-supplied preset.exampleLink to an anchor with target=_blank and rel="noopener noreferrer". That link can lead to the 11 allowlisted hosts in apps/web-app/src/shared/example-link.ts:15-27, including X, Reddit, Instagram, pixiv, Bluesky, misskey.io, Eorzea Collection, Mirapri and the Lodestone. sanitizeExampleLink (example-link.ts:56-63) enforces https and the allowlist on the read path. Neither the 2026-08-29 nor the 2026-09-15 audit report mentions example links, and docs/architecture/security-trade-offs.md does not either, so this is not a previously accepted or rejected item.

Why it does not reach LOW:
- Nothing the documents say is false. The URL carries nothing about the visitor, the referrer is suppressed, and the click is a visible, deliberate navigation to a link the preset's author chose.

So this is a completeness gap in the documents, not a statement that misleads the reader. It is still worth one CORRECT sentence, since presets can now send users to social sites the section never names. My grade is INFO, INTERNET-UNAUTH (anyone can read the policy and open a public preset), policy CORRECT, reconcile_case 3, rotation NONE.

It also needs a Discord id that no local account owns, which in practice means a Discord account that has never signed in here. Signing in with that new Discord account directly would already give one more vote and one fresh quota. So the double vote and the quota reset add nothing beyond the Sybil voting that is already free.
- **The main harm falls on the user.** A legitimate user loses self-service edit, delete and "my submissions" for their pre-link presets.

All 31 FINDINGs of 2026-08-29 hold at HEAD, each with a located control and a passing guard test. 62 guard test files were run singly, 0 failures. Results are in evidence/scripts/regression/results.txt and results2.txt.

Bot signing: v1 is gone and v2 is enforced. Presets-api auth.ts:309-340 verifies v2, does a KV nonce replay check (botnonce:, 120 s) and rejects unsigned bot calls outside dev. The canonical string is length-prefixed (auth hmac.ts:276-291). HMAC keys must be >= 32 bytes (hmac.ts:99-101). The signature window is 60 s (hmac.ts:323-336). JWT alg is pinned to HS256 (jwt.ts:147).

Discord interactions: the timestamp freshness check precedes the body read (auth discord.ts:100-119). Every moderation-worker command, button, modal and autocomplete calls isModerator, and presets-api re-checks via requireModerator.

Body caps are streamed everywhere user-reachable: oauth 10 KB, presets-api 100 KB (5 MB for preview upload, plus a magic-byte sniff at presets.ts:1177), Discord 100,000 B, GitHub 1 MiB, telemetry 16 KB. All use Hono bodyLimit or an explicit reader with cancel.

Telemetry: client default-off (toggleOn=false at telemetry-service.ts:53) with a GPC gate at :118. Server-side exact-Origin allowlist plus Sec-GPC -> 204 with no trace (api-worker telemetry/router.ts:57-70, origin.ts).

reviews.label: trust-boundaries
positive_controls: Service bindings: image-worker has no public surface (workers_dev=false, preview_urls=false, no routes) and refuses *.workers.dev hosts (apps/image-worker/src/index.ts:112-119). presets-api and api-worker are public but authenticated by bearer secret, v2 HMAC and a single-use nonce (apps/presets-api/src/middleware/auth.ts:269-343), or public by design.

Outbound: every target is a constant or operator var with a timeout. The user-reachable fetches have strong SSRF controls: image-worker validators.ts:25-27,160-215,423-475 (exact Discord CDN host set, redirect manual with one revalidated hop, 10 MB streamed cap) and chara-attachment.ts:23-108. Universalis uses a 5 MB streamed cap.
Path inputs are encoded or validated: encodeURIComponent on preset ids and world, Universalis datacenter whitelist plus digit-only ids, canonical-decimal icon id.
Cache keys use fixed synthetic origins and canonicalised ids. No KV or Cache API key is built from free text. The og cache uses a query-key allowlist.
Error handlers never return a stack or env value in production. Every dev branch lives on an unrouted workers_dev=false worker.
oauth, moderation-worker and api-worker error paths send no-store. CORS allowlists are exact-match with dev loopback gated on ENVIRONMENT.
No secrets in [vars]; .dev.vars* are gitignored and none are tracked. Side effects use waitUntil. Module-scope state is isolate-local rate-limit or public-cache data only.
No scheduled/queue/cron handlers or Durable Objects exist anywhere.
rejected: Universalis proxy per-isolate MemoryRateLimiter (c1 in my first draft): already an accepted trade-off in the 2026-08-29 report's Rejected list and PKG-11. Nothing relevant changed since 0332fcc5 (only 3e6d9a46 and 6fce09cf touched it). The missing security-trade-offs.md entry goes to handoffs.

No no-store on presets-api authenticated JSON: already PAPI-15/PAPI-11 INFO, unchanged, and presets-api index.ts has no commits since 0332fcc5. Cloudflare does not cache JSON by default. The 2026-09-15 positive-control wording overstates presets-api.

v2 bot signature does not bind the query string: FINDING-015 (2026-08-29) records it as deliberately not done and INFO. It needs an in-path position, the nonce is single-use, and a binding offers no capture position.

Service-binding callers skipping the presets-api IP limiter when CF-Connecting-IP is absent: Cloudflare sets that header on every external request, so the skip is unreachable from the internet; callers are limited per authenticated user instead.

Unpinned preview_urls on presets-api, oauth, moderation-worker, og-worker and discord-worker production: wrangler passes undefined and the platform default follows workers_dev=false (wrangler cli.js:159906-159915, :160021). Not verifiable without Cloudflare.
Beta discord-worker (workers_dev=true) bound to production presets-api, api-worker and image-worker: documented accepted residual risk (DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENTS.md:255-256).
presets-api CORS lists xiv-colorexplorer.pages.dev: auth is a bearer token in per-origin storage with no cookies, so a claimed origin gains nothing. This is the unchanged PAPI-11 INFO.
Dev-mode err.message/stack in presets-api, oauth and moderation-worker onError: only when ENVIRONMENT=development, and those workers have no routes and workers_dev=false.
notFound handlers echo c.req.path in JSON (presets-api, oauth, api-worker): application/json with nosniff, so no HTML sink.
discord-worker unauthorizedResponse(error) echoes the verifier reason: fixed strings or a library message, no secret or internal path.
Request-ID header injection: the request ID is UUID-validated (request-id.ts:47-56).
Host-header trust: oauth builds all URLs from env; api-worker and og-worker use the host only to choose a static-asset or redirect branch with fixed targets.
og-worker fetch(request) SSRF: gated to the app host, 5 s timeout, same-origin target.
D1 template SQL: only a switch-whitelisted ORDER BY plus ? placeholders.
Docs live explorer fetching arbitrary URLs: API_BASE is a constant.
KV key collision between jti revocation and botnonce: the nonce key is written only after HMAC verification and is pattern-limited.
scheduled/queue/Durable Object handlers: none exist.

critic.notes:
I did not re-review findings. I diffed coverage, matched handoffs against the reviews that should have picked them up, and grepped siblings. Every assignment returned, so none needs re-issuing. The file-coverage diff used basenames, which can hide gaps where names collide, so I re-matched the names that collide (og-worker translator.ts/fonts.ts, index/types/router, the discord-worker contrast/harmony/mixer-v4 handlers) against their unit paths. The only security-relevant file nobody read is og-worker translator.ts. Its slug echo (getLocalizedClanOrRace) is reached only after the isKnownClanOrRace own-property check (the FINDING-024 fix), so no gap.

Negatives I checked and closed:
- No scheduled(), queue, Durable Object, cron or [triggers] in any wrangler.toml or worker src.
- No ENVIRONMENT/development relaxations in packages/{auth,worker-kit,logger} or og-worker src. discord-worker's only ENVIRONMENT branch adds production-only checks (env-validation.ts:112). This closes the ci-supply-chain handoff about the beta bot on workers.dev.
- api-worker's [[kv_namespaces]] is RATE_LIMIT, the KV fallback limiter the policy discloses (120 s), not a cache.
- The presets-api and oauth MemoryRateLimiter instances are fallbacks used only when the native binding is absent, consistent with PRIVACY.md :139-144. Only the universalis one is always on (already pii-web#c4).
- The five .chara fixtures under packages/core/src/services/chara/__tests__/fixtures have Author and Description null and no Nickname key (closes the ci-supply-chain privacy handoff).
- EXIF is closed: image-worker re-encodes to WebP (review-presets-api.md:45, review-packages-security.md:47).
- The web-app file.name/producer logging is console-only and dev-gated.
- The presets-api pages.dev and projectgalatine CORS origins were already rejected (review-trust-boundaries.md:110), so not re-issued.
- All five locale variants of all four documents were read, and policy-locale-parity.txt PASSES.
- The api-worker docs site's v-html sinks are static (api-worker-public#c1 was rejected).
- The rows of the Step 3 checklist (Hono, Discord bots, oauth, presets-api, image-worker, og/api-worker, web-app, packages, CI) each have evidence in the review files. Freshness, v1 removal, the canonical string, constant-time compare, decompression gate, cache keys, no-store, CORS and SSRF timeouts are all cited at file:line.

Dropped as low value:
- The og-worker/packages-svg generator full read: inputs are allowlisted ints, hex and enums, and two reviewers already swept for escapeXml.
- presets-api scripts/migrate-presets.ts: local seed script, no secrets.
- api-worker lib/api-error.ts and regional-names.ts: the onError path was read.

Open handoffs that are plain bugs or docs, not coverage gaps, left for the coordinator's appendix:
- presets-api `search` length and `page` bounds (500s)
- notifyDiscordBot has no AbortSignal
- the image-worker /extract JSON cap

gaps.brief: Two handoffs about the preset author name were never picked up. (1) apps/discord-worker/src/services/preset-api.ts sets the X-User-Discord-Name header to the raw Discord display name (global_name ?? username). A Worker Headers value must be a ByteString, so a name containing characters above U+00FF (any Japanese, Korean or Chinese display name) may make `new Request(...)`/`headers.set` throw. That would break /preset submit and edit for CJK users, which the six-language audience makes a real population. Verify in workerd/miniflare: a probe under evidence/scripts is fine, and so is an existing vitest-pool-workers test. Also check whether the v2 HMAC canonical string (which includes the name) and presets-api auth.ts:254 handle the value the same way on both ends. Do the same check for moderation-worker's bot requests. (2) This is the sibling of the confirmed presets-api#c5 (example_link stored raw, skipping the control/bidi rule): `author_name` is written to D1 from auth.userName (presets.ts:354-364 refresh-author, ~962, ~1029, ~1245). As far as the coordinator can see, it gets no length cap and no control/zero-width/bidi stripping, while name and description do (validation-service.ts). Confirm, then list every sink that renders author_name and say whether each one sanitizes: web Lit templates, Discord embeds via sanitizeEmbedText, moderation-worker embeds, any API consumer. Out of scope: username-vs-display-name wording (pii-bot#c4 was REJECTED; policy-web-en#c3 and policy-bot-en#c3 are already CONFIRMED). Return candidates in the usual table with file:line.

gaps.label: gap2-beta-deploy-actors-vs-prod-trust
gaps.scope: .github/workflows/deploy-web-app-beta.yml, deploy-og-worker-beta.yml, deploy-discord-worker-beta.yml; GitHub repo settings via `gh api` (environments beta and copilot, deployment branch policies, collaborators, Copilot coding agent / Actions settings, rulesets on non-main branches); apps/oauth/src/constants/oauth.ts (10-48 ALLOWED_REDIRECT_ORIGINS); apps/presets-api/wrangler.toml (ADDITIONAL_CORS_ORIGINS); apps/web-app/src/services/auth-service.ts (token storage); docs/architecture/security-trade-offs.md; docs/audits/2026-10-03-security/evidence/review-ci-supply-chain.md and review-web-app-shell.md (handoff sections)
gaps.brief: Two handoffs point at the same boundary and nobody owned both. web-app-shell noted that https://beta.xivdyetools.app is a PRODUCTION oauth redirect origin and production presets-api CORS origin, so production auth codes and JWTs go to whatever beta build is live. deploy-web-app-beta.yml deploys it on a push to ANY non-main branch except dependabot/**, using `environment: beta`, which has no branch policy and no reviewers. ci-supply-chain recorded that a `copilot` GitHub environment was created on 2026-09-28 with no workflow, and asked whether the Copilot agent is intended and whether its branches can trigger the beta deploys. The earlier residual (INF-06, '2026-08-29 FINDING-028 fixed class') rested on 'only the owner can push'. Establish the CURRENT set of actors who can make a non-main branch push or a workflow_dispatch that runs deploy-web-app-beta.yml: owner, the Copilot coding agent (copilot/** branches, which issue text can drive), GitHub Apps, bots. If an actor other than the maintainer can do it, the beta site becomes a way to harvest production sessions (a malicious beta build reads the production JWT from storage or receives the production code). File it with severity and exposure decided by who that actor is. If only the maintainer can push, record a positive control and stop. Do not re-file oauth#c1 (retired projectgalatine origin), the presets-api pages.dev CORS origin (already rejected in review-trust-boundaries.md:110), or the FINDING-028 token separation.

gaps.label: gap2-identity-link-blast-radius
gaps.scope: apps/presets-api/src/middleware/auth.ts (55-77 resolveJWTUserId); apps/presets-api/src/middleware/ban-check.ts (30-60); apps/presets-api/src/handlers/votes.ts; apps/presets-api/src/handlers/presets.ts (owner PATCH/DELETE, my-submissions, refresh-author ~340-370); apps/presets-api/src/services/{preset-service,rate-limit-service}.ts; apps/presets-api/schema.sql + migrations (votes unique key, submission_events); apps/oauth/src/services/user-service.ts (183-200 attachIdentities); apps/web-app/PRIVACY.md and TERMS_OF_SERVICE.md (removal/ownership text); docs/architecture/security-trade-offs.md
gaps.brief: Sibling of the confirmed delta-commits#c2. An XIVAuth-only user's acting id is their oauth UUID (`sub`). When oauth later stamps a linked discord_id on the account (user-service.ts:183-200), resolveJWTUserId switches to the Discord snowflake. #c2 covers only the ban table. The ban-check.ts comment adds that the user's 'UUID-authored presets also stop being theirs', calling it 'pre-existing, not new', but no reviewer followed the other id-keyed paths. For each query keyed on the resolved id, state what happens across the switch, with file:line: (a) votes: can the same person vote twice on one preset, once per id; check the unique constraint; (b) the daily submission/edit cap in submission_events: does linking reset it; (c) owner edit/delete/my-submissions: after linking, can the user still see, edit or DELETE presets they authored? If not, this is a data-subject rights failure on top of a bug, since the web policy routes removal through the maintainer; (d) refresh-author leaves UUID-authored rows with the old name; (e) the reverse direction, if any. Check whether docs/architecture/security-trade-offs.md lists this as an accepted trade-off. A code comment alone is not acceptance. Exclude the ban case itself (delta-commits#c2). Fold findings into #c2 if they share its fix.

gaps.brief: The bot policy §7 promises 'To request deletion of all your data ... We will process deletion requests within 30 days.' review-policy-bot-en.md:73 marked this UNVERIFIABLE and passed it on as documentation only (handoff at :100), so check (c)/(f) of the Privacy-policies-accuracy row was never done for it. Check whether the promise can be kept for each store holding the Discord user id: (1) Analytics Engine datapoints with the user id as a blob (analytics.ts). Analytics Engine has no per-row delete, and rows stay for about 3 months, so 'all your data within 30 days' looks false unless a caveat exists; quote what §7/§8 say. (2) Copies posted to Discord moderation/log channels (author name, mention, preset text). (3) KV `usertrack:<date>:<id>`, `firstrun:v5:<id>` and the legacy `i18n:user:` / `budget:world:v1:` keys: can an operator find and delete them from the id alone? (4) D1 votes/submission_events/moderation_log. Produce a store-by-store table: deletable by the operator on request (yes/no, how), and what the policy says. File a candidate only where the policy promises something the stores cannot do or stays silent about a store that survives a deletion request. Confirm the five translations make the same promise. Do not re-file pii-bot#c3, policy-bot-en#c5 or moderation-worker#c2 (ban-record disclosure/retention), discord-worker-core#c1 (/preferences reset legacy keys) or the web-side pii-web#c8; policy-web-en#c2 (web removal path) was rejected.

gaps.label: gap3-dev-dependency-advisories
gaps.scope: pnpm-lock.yaml; pnpm-workspace.yaml (overrides); apps/*/package.json and packages/*/package.json devDependencies; apps/api-worker/docs/.vitepress/** (VitePress/Vue client bundle served on developers.xivdyetools.app); .github/workflows/{deploy-*.yml,publish-packages.yml,sync-dye-emojis.yml}; docs/audits/2026-10-03-security/evidence/pnpm-audit.json
gaps.brief:
This gap measures current exposure. It does not re-file ci-supply-chain#c3, which already confirmed that the only advisory gate is `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level high`. No review has run an audit that includes devDependencies or moderate severity. The collector's prod audit (evidence/pnpm-audit.json) reports totalDependencies: 27 and devDependencies: 0 across nine apps and eight packages.

Steps:
(1) Sanity-check the existing gate. Compare that 27 with `pnpm ls --prod -r --depth Infinity` and confirm the prod audit enumerates every workspace importer, including hono, lit, @resvg/resvg-wasm, @cf-wasm/photon and revolt.js. If it does not, the gate under-reports even for shipped runtime code.
(2) Run `pnpm audit --json` read-only (all deps, all severities) from the repo root. Save the output only under your scratch directory.
(3) Triage every advisory into two classes that matter:
  (a) DevDeps whose code ships to users. VitePress and Vue are compiled into the static docs site at developers.xivdyetools.app. Also check for any Vite plugin or PostCSS/Tailwind step that injects runtime code into the web-app bundle.
  (b) DevDeps that execute inside secret-holding CI jobs. These are wrangler under CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN in every deploy-*.yml, vite and its plugins in deploy-web-app.yml, vitepress in deploy-api-worker.yml, tsup/esbuild in publish-packages.yml under `id-token: write` (npm OIDC), and tsx in sync-dye-emojis.yml under the bot token.
  For each advisory, decide whether the vulnerable code path is reachable in that use. For example, a dev-server-only vite advisory is not reachable in `vite build`.
(4) Check whether the security-floor overrides in pnpm-workspace.yaml (rollup, qs, seroval, vitepress>vite, tsup>esbuild) still resolve to patched versions in the lockfile.

Report candidates only for advisories that are reachable in class (a) or (b). Record unreachable ones as rejected, with the reason.
